rows.requirement: Offer one simple interface: a web chat, a command line or a messaging bot.
rows.how: The `aksha` command line and an HTTP server (`aksha serve`) both drive one session API; a web app (`aksha serve --web`) and a chat terminal UI (`aksha chat`) are clients of the same API.

evidence.expect: lists demo, run, answer, approve, reject, status, inspect and the other subcommands

rows.requirement: Let the user pick an agent by name or describe the request and have the harness route it.
rows.how: A named agent skips the classifier; otherwise the router classifies the request by each loaded agent's declared purpose.

rows.requirement: Show which agent handles the request.
rows.how: The route decision is recorded and the reply is labelled with the chosen agent.

rows.requirement: Ask for clarification when the request is unclear.
rows.how: When the classifier abstains or fails, the router raises a route question instead of guessing.

rows.requirement: The harness calls the model and runs tools.
rows.how: One loop runs every agent: a model turn, then each tool call through the policy gate and the durable executor.

rows.requirement: Keep conversation history and separate user sessions.
rows.how: Every command and model step is an event in the store, keyed by owner and session; a resumed run continues its own session.

rows.requirement: Control which tools each agent can use.
rows.how: Each agent lists its tools; the policy gate denies by default and checks every call against the agent's permissions.

rows.requirement: Handle errors, timeouts and execution limits.
rows.how: Each step has a timeout and a bounded retry policy, and each run has a budget of model turns, tool calls and active time.

rows.requirement: Record what happened during a run.
rows.how: The hash-chained event store is the record; the inspector, `aksha status` and the trace export are projections of it.

rows.requirement: Ask for approval before sending documents through a mock service.
rows.how: `send_packet` needs an approval bound to the exact packet version by signature, and the send goes through the outbox to a mock mailbox.

rows.requirement: Save conversations, workflow checkpoints, artifacts and pending approvals so they survive a restart.
rows.how: All of these are events or versioned artifacts in the store, so a restarted process rebuilds them and resumes.

rows.requirement: Each agent defines its purpose, instructions and allowed tools, separate from the shared runtime.
rows.how: An agent is a data definition in its own package: Tasks, prompts, tool list and limits, loaded and hashed by one loader.

rows.requirement: A new agent can be added without editing the runtime.
rows.how: Test fixture agents load through the same extension API, and a test checks the runtime's hash does not change when a third agent is added.

rows.requirement: Use one fictional venture: a camera-free room occupancy sensor.
rows.how: The `stillroom` world is that venture; every input is synthetic and labelled so in its own content.

rows.requirement: Create four invention candidates (self-calibration, sensor placement, privacy-preserving coordination, battery-saving sampling) with technical mechanisms.
rows.how: One engineering note per candidate states its problem, mechanism steps and alternatives.

rows.requirement: Include engineering notes, contributor records, dated disclosure history, business priorities and blank disclosure templates.
rows.how: Each kind is its own input file in the world.

rows.requirement: Add competitor pages, customer reviews and patent-publication fixtures, clearly labelled as synthetic, with no invented number presented as a real patent.
rows.how: Vendor pages live on the world's offline web; publications use `SYN-PUB-` identifiers and each file carries a synthetic label.

rows.requirement: Limit the core exercise to five competitors and five patent families.
rows.how: The answer key counts five resolved competitors on six pages and five families over ten publications.

rows.requirement: Establish the customer segment, geography and research boundary, asking only material questions.
rows.how: The `scope` Task saves segment, geography and boundary with where each value came from, and asks only for a value the request leaves open.

rows.requirement: Search for competing products and manual alternatives, and resolve company identity and duplicates.
rows.how: The `discover` Task merges pages into one company only on a stated relationship; manual alternatives are searched and, when none is found, saved as an explicit unknown.
rows.reason: The bundled worlds hold no page describing a manual alternative, so only the not-found path is tested.

rows.requirement: Fetch product and pricing pages; search snippets alone do not support a claim.
rows.how: A search mints no citable span, and grounding refuses a citation to a search hit.

rows.requirement: Query mock customer reviews or keyword data, preserving source IDs, dates, geography and units.
rows.how: Reviews are read one passage per row with their IDs and dates, and prices keep amount, currency and terms.

rows.requirement: Separate facts, vendor claims, inferences and unknowns, and keep conflicting findings visible.
rows.how: Every claim carries a label, and two pages that disagree are saved side by side with a conflict relation.

rows.requirement: Produce a competitor matrix and a source list linking each finding to its exact supporting excerpt.
rows.how: Every matrix cell cites a span whose text is checked against the stored page at its offsets, or is an explicit unknown.

rows.requirement: Propose one small customer experiment with thresholds labelled as proposals.
rows.how: The report check refuses a test whose thresholds are not marked as proposals.

rows.requirement: Do not treat reviews or search interest as proof of demand, or infer market prevalence from a small sample.
rows.how: Findings must be stated as N of M in this sample, and no output may state a market share.

rows.requirement: Required outputs: competitor table, linked source list, deduplicated customer findings, one proposed test.
rows.how: The run completes only when its four outputs exist at current versions.

rows.requirement: Extract each invention's problem, mechanism, alternatives, contributors and disclosure history from the notes.
rows.how: `extract[Cn]` saves an extraction where every graded fact carries its exact quote.

rows.requirement: Ask targeted questions about missing technical details and never invent an answer.
rows.how: A value the note leaves undecided raises an input question on that candidate only; the field stays unknown until answered.

rows.requirement: Search related references and fetch publication text, including independent claims.
rows.how: `search_publications` and `fetch_publication` read the uploaded publications, claims included.

rows.requirement: Group related publications into families and keep material differences between members.
rows.how: Families are grouped by shared priority numbers, with each member kept.

rows.requirement: Record publication identifiers, dates, source URLs and status wording exactly as stated.
rows.how: Status wording is kept verbatim, and two differing statuses stay visible.

rows.requirement: Build a feature-by-reference matrix that separates overlap from missing features.
rows.how: `compare` saves one cell per mechanism step and family with a state of `disclosed`, `partial`, `not_found` or `not_checked`.
rows.reason: The matrix equals the key on the bundled worlds, but the offline comparison counts words, so some held-out worlds get wrong cells (limitations item 19); a live model is the fix.

rows.requirement: Compare business importance, implementation evidence, distinctions, closest prior art and risks, and give one next action per candidate.
rows.how: A rule table picks `prioritize_counsel_review`, `collect_more_evidence` or `deprioritize_for_now`, and a check vetoes any action the rules do not give.

rows.requirement: Explain tradeoffs and what new evidence would change each recommendation, without an unexplained score.
rows.how: Each recommendation states why, its risks and what would change it; no score field exists.

rows.requirement: Use Research Agent outputs through explicit artifact IDs and versions, not as proof of novelty.
rows.how: The `recommend` Task declares reads of `research.needs` and `research.findings` by kind, so each recommendation's lineage records the exact versions read; it cites them as artifact cites (`research.needs@v2`) under `business_importance` only, with a note that research is not evidence of novelty. The check refuses a research output named anywhere else; run alone, business importance from research is unknown; a research rebuild reopens every recommendation that read it.

rows.requirement: Show each candidate's recommendation with sources, concerns and missing information.
rows.how: `table` gathers every recommendation with its citations, risks and missing documents.

rows.requirement: Ask the user which candidates to prepare and save the selection before continuing.
rows.how: `select` raises a choice interrupt and saves the selection before any form is filled.

rows.requirement: Fill a structured invention disclosure and a mock filing-information worksheet through a tool.
rows.how: `fill_form` writes each field against the blank template, which decides what is required.

rows.requirement: Include technical explanation, alternatives, source references, contributors and dated disclosure history in the forms.
rows.how: Every template field is reported, and contributor fields carry counsel flags where needed.

rows.requirement: Add a figure list, prior-art matrix, unresolved questions and coverage directions phrased as questions for counsel.
rows.how: The disclosure template requires `figure_list` and `open_questions_for_counsel`, and the packet opens with a counsel section.

rows.requirement: Validate required fields and report each as complete, missing or needing counsel confirmation.
rows.how: A field cannot be marked complete when it needs counsel, and a missing required field keeps the packet from ready.

rows.requirement: Save a versioned counsel-review packet and keep unknowns rather than guessing.
rows.how: Every artifact version is immutable, and the packet check needs the counsel section first.

rows.requirement: Request separate approval before a simulated external handoff; selection does not authorise sending.
rows.how: Selecting a candidate creates no approval; `send_packet` asks for its own.

rows.requirement: Give no patentability or freedom-to-operate opinion, no final claims, no legal deadlines and no filing.
rows.how: The instructions forbid them and a test scans every output for forbidden content; date facts are dates and day counts only.

rows.requirement: Required outputs: a recommendation table for all four candidates, comparison matrix, saved selection, completed forms and packets.
rows.how: The patent happy-path case checks each output against the world's key.

rows.requirement: Describe each workflow's states, dependencies, completion checks and approval points, and why.
rows.how: Each agent's Task tree, reads and checks are declared in its definition and explained in its module docstring and the design records.
rows.reason: The design is written down, but it cannot be shown to have come before the code.

rows.requirement: Execute tool calls; tool results affect the next step.
rows.how: The model sees each tool result before its next call.

rows.requirement: Track completed steps, blockers, source versions and the next action.
rows.how: The scheduler's status is a projection of the store, equal to a full rebuild.

evidence.expect: each run's state, open interrupts and next step

rows.requirement: Pause for missing information or approval, then resume from that state.
rows.how: A question or approval holds the run; an answer or grant resumes it.

rows.requirement: Keep evidence and saved outputs linked to their inputs.
rows.how: Every saved version records the reads and citations it rests on.

rows.requirement: When inputs change, mark affected findings and approvals stale and recheck them before further action.
rows.how: Invalidation marks dependent versions invalidated or dirty and revokes approvals on invalidated targets.

rows.requirement: Preserve unaffected work and explain what needs to run again.
rows.how: Only the dependents of a moved input are rebuilt, and the rebuild plan names each one with its cause.

rows.requirement: Return a partial result when evidence is insufficient; do not manufacture completion.
rows.how: A run with a gap ends `partial` with the gap named, never `complete`.

rows.requirement: Save Research Agent outputs with IDs and versions so the Patent Agent can read and cite them.
rows.how: Research outputs are versioned artifacts; the patent agent's `recommend` Task reads them by kind and cites each by ID and version.

evidence.expect: lists each saved output as kind@version

rows.requirement: Keep both agents separate, not one long prompt.
rows.how: Each agent has its own definition and context; the patent context holds no research run's turns or tool results, only the research outputs a Task declares it reads, as versioned artifacts.

rows.requirement: Provide executable mock adapters for document reading, search, page and publication fetching, review queries, form writing and artifact storage.
rows.how: Shared input and web tools, the patent domain tools and `save_artifact` all run offline against a world.

rows.requirement: Add a mock document-sending tool that cannot send without approval.
rows.how: `send_packet` without an approval writes no outbox entry.

rows.requirement: Enforce each agent's allowed operations in code.
rows.how: Architecture tests prove no tool body runs without a gate allow.

rows.requirement: Save workflow progress and draft documents automatically.
rows.how: A save commits with its step, so a rerun replays it.

rows.requirement: Include a deterministic fixture or replay mode and a fake-model mode; run with no paid credentials or network.
rows.how: Offline, every model is a rule-based fake; a recorded run replays with no model and no network.

evidence.expect: exits 0 with no API key and no network

rows.requirement: Document optional live search and model adapters without committing secrets.
rows.how: Live mode reads keys from the environment and refuses to start without them.

rows.requirement: Set and enforce tool-call limits, timeouts and bounded retries.
rows.how: Budgets cap tool calls and turns per run; each tool has a `RetryPolicy` with a timeout and a retry cap.

rows.requirement: Make fixtures replaceable so the workflow works on changed inputs, not a scripted transcript.
rows.how: Both agents run on eleven worlds of different shapes, six written without sight of the code.
rows.reason: On the held-out worlds the research agent passes 25 of 26 cases and the patent agent 17 of 24 in fake model mode (limitations item 19).

rows.requirement: Enforce tool permissions in code, not only in prompts.
rows.how: The gate is pure code over the agent definition and holds no model text.

rows.requirement: Keep users' conversations and data separate.
rows.how: Every store read, upload folder and stream is keyed by owner.

rows.requirement: Treat documents and tool results as data, not instructions that change permissions.
rows.how: Instruction-like text is flagged; a world with injected text gives the same gate decisions as a clean one.

rows.requirement: Show the exact action for approval; rejection changes nothing; an edited action needs fresh approval.
rows.how: The approval shows its action and signature; a reject writes no effect; any change to the action changes the signature.

rows.requirement: Prevent retries from creating duplicate records or sends.
rows.how: Saves and sends are keyed by meaning; a retry returns the first result.

rows.requirement: Keep secrets out of code and logs.
rows.how: Keys come from the environment, go only in request headers and are dropped from provider error messages.

rows.requirement: Connect no real company accounts; use mock services and fake-model mode.
rows.how: The only system of record is a development mailbox in a JSON file.

rows.requirement: Automated tests cover both agents, adding a plugin, blocked tool access, user isolation, approvals and restart recovery.
rows.how: Each area has its own test files, run by `make test`.

rows.requirement: Duplicate competitor results and patent-family members do not inflate outputs.
rows.how: Pages merge into one company, reviews are counted once, and family members group under one family.

rows.requirement: Conflicting pricing or publication statuses stay visible with their sources.
rows.how: Both values are saved with their citations and a conflict relation.

rows.requirement: Missing data stays unknown, not zero; a failed fetch stays unverified.
rows.how: Grounding refuses a zero where the value is missing and marks a failed fetch unverified.

rows.requirement: A fetched document that tells the agent to change permissions or bypass approval has no effect.
rows.how: A model that obeys the page is refused by the gate and nothing changes.

rows.requirement: A tool timeout, exhausted retries or the tool-call limit keeps useful partial work.
rows.how: The step ends in an error, the budget raises an interrupt, and finalisation saves a partial result from the reserve.

rows.requirement: A rejected approval causes no action; an edited action needs fresh approval.
rows.how: See the approval row under safeguards; the command line keeps the run waiting after a refusal.

rows.requirement: A restart during a write or simulated handoff does not duplicate the effect.
rows.how: A kill at every commit point recovers to one result per step and one send per packet version.

rows.requirement: Insufficient evidence blocks readiness even when the user asks to mark a candidate complete.
rows.how: Insisting does not unblock a check, and `fill_form` refuses to mark a counsel field complete.

groups.title: The change-and-recovery demo, sentence by sentence

rows.requirement: Run both agents on the fictional venture.
rows.how: Act 1 of `aksha demo` runs the research and patent agents on `stillroom` to `complete`.

rows.requirement: Select a patent candidate and prepare its draft documents.
rows.how: The scripted person selects C1; its forms and packet are filled and the packet is sent once under an approval.

rows.requirement: Introduce a closer prior-art reference and reveal an external contributor to the key mechanism.
rows.how: The change adds `SYN-PUB-0011` (family E, which discloses C1's two gates) and moves the outside consultant's email to a date before the consulting agreement took effect.
rows.reason: The outside contributor is already in the base inputs; the change re-dates the email so the contribution predates the agreement, rather than adding a person the first run never saw.

rows.requirement: Restart the application.
rows.how: The demo closes its runtime after the rebuild and kills a child process with SIGKILL mid-send; recovery runs in a fresh runtime.
rows.reason: In the demo the restart comes after the rebuild, during the send; a restart between the change and the rebuild is covered by tests, not shown in the demo.

rows.requirement: Reopen affected comparisons, forms and recommendations.
rows.how: Invalidation reopens C1's extraction, prior art, comparison, recommendation, forms and packet.

rows.requirement: Flag contribution and ownership questions for counsel.
rows.how: The outside contribution is saved `needs_counsel_confirmation` with inventorship and ownership questions.

rows.requirement: Invalidate affected approvals and request fresh approval.
rows.how: The new packet version has a new signature, so the old approval does not cover it and a fresh one is asked for.

rows.requirement: Preserve unaffected research and prevent duplicate records or sends.
rows.how: Research outputs the change did not reach are kept, and the mailbox holds one delivery per packet version.

rows.requirement: Explain the revised result using the new evidence.
rows.how: C1's next action moves from `prioritize_counsel_review` to `collect_more_evidence` because family E discloses two of its steps, and the packet's diff review shows what changed.

rows.requirement: Make each run inspectable: agent, state, tool calls, input versions, approvals, outputs and errors.
rows.how: The inspector and `aksha status` read all of these from the store without booting a run.

evidence.expect: the run's agent, state, steps, reads, approvals and outputs

rows.requirement: A repository with clear setup and test commands.
rows.how: The README and Makefile give one-command setup, tests and the demo.

rows.requirement: A short README on the architecture and how to add an agent.
rows.how: The README links to the architecture overview and the extension API record.

rows.requirement: All fictional fixtures, blank templates, expected-output examples and example conversations.
rows.how: Each world ships its inputs and an answer key; one recorded run holds a whole conversation with its outputs.

rows.requirement: Workflow state diagrams or tables, tool schemas and the decision rules.
rows.how: The rule table is code, tool schemas are declared in each tool and snapshotted, and the approval states are in their record.

rows.requirement: Structured JSON outputs plus readable summaries; each recommendation traces to its evidence.
rows.how: Every output is a JSON artifact that names its citations; `aksha show` prints them.

evidence.expect: lists the saved outputs; with an ID, prints one as JSON

rows.requirement: A short demo of both agents, an approval and the change-and-recovery scenario.
rows.how: `aksha demo` runs all of it offline in about 20 seconds and exits 0 only when every check passes.

rows.how: Each limitation is numbered and dated.
